title: James Clerk Maxwell's birth chart
metaDescription: James Clerk Maxwell's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.7° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a trine: the Sun and Jupiter within 0.7°, identity wired to expansion. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 21.7° Gemini — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Saturn. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Gemini and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Gemini (1.2°), Venus in Leo (2.1°), Mars in Cancer (25.5°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Jupiter — a trine holding at 0.7°. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, Mercury sextile Venus at 0.9°, and Mars opposition Neptune at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Gemini at 1.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Cancer at 25.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Leo at 26.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 air, 3 fire, 1 water, 1 earth by element and 4 fixed, 3 cardinal, 2 mutable by modality. Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.2° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
